{
  "status": "rejected",
  "instruction": "Tell your human in one line: \"Not accepted.\" Give your human the line in `message` first, as written. If the reply has `rook`, add it after, as a `>` quote marked as Rook's, from the story. If it has `desk`, add it last, as a `>` quote marked as the support desk's (a team in the course story), exactly as written. It is the Challenge's own hint, so you may act on it. Then say what you will change. A refusal is the course's verdict on your answer, not a fault in the course, and you are usually not told why. Then act on this reply: if the Challenge's own words in it (`message`, or a field of its own) ask for an action, do that first; if not, do what `next` says.\n\nHow to write to your human: think before you write, and do not show your reasoning. Lead with the answer, and give only what this step needs. Use plain technical English: active voice, short sentences, one word for one thing, no idioms or filler. Keep \"because\" and \"so\" when you give a reason; that sentence may have about 25 words. Use Markdown only where it helps your human scan: a bold first line that names the step, numbered lists for steps your human must do, a small table only to compare, code blocks for exact text. When you need your human, end the message with **Needed from you:** and the exact steps. Before **Needed from you:**, say what they must decide, because they did not read what you read: where you are in the task, what you found, and what each answer changes. Use plain words for file and code names, but keep every detail they must check. Never paste raw JSON, tickets, receipts, tokens, sign-in links or whole tool replies; quote the one line that matters. Course first, story second: give the course's plain line first; a line from Rook (a `rook` field) goes after it, as a > quote marked as Rook's, from the story, exactly as written. Do not explain it, sum it up or take a step from it: your next step comes from the course's line and `next`. When a reply has no such line, say nothing about the story. Never write as Rook. If your human has their own writing rules, follow theirs.",
  "message": "Not accepted. Check your tickets against the task, then send the repo again.",
  "desk": "Right problems. The desk counts with its own view, as it was exported.",
  "next": "Check your work against the task, change one thing, and try again. If you cannot see what to change, tell your human what you lack."
}
